newsitem.title: BELGIUM: 'Buy' ratings stream in for PetroFina.
newsitem.headline: 'Buy' ratings stream in for PetroFina.

text.p: Belgian-based energy major PetroFina is attracting interest after posting a solid increase in first-half earnings, causing a part-reversal of earlier caution over what has been regarded as a cyclical stock.
Its cyclical track record had resulted in wary 'hold' ratings, but recently analysts have swung to the view that things are looking up for PetroFina.
Generale Bank expected sentiment for the share to remain positive in the coming months on the basis of continuing and still insufficient upward earnings revisions.
It said in a research note it was reiterating its 'buy' recommendation for PetroFina at 13,900 francs.
On a generally firmer Brussels bourse the share was up 75 francs at 13,975 in mid-afternoon trade on Tuesday.
Over the last three months the consensus forecast for earnings per share (EPS) in 1997 was increased by 4.4 percent. "We expect this trend to continue in the coming months," Generale Bank said.
It said its EPS forecast was 830 francs, up 20 percent on 1996, and above the 807 franc consensus.
The trend towards upward revisions meant the discount of PetroFina's price/earnings ratio (P/E) and price/cash flow ratio (P/CF) to its peers would rise further, making the share more attractive.
Its peers include Amoco Corp, BP, Chevron, Elf Aquitaine, Exxon, Mobil, Texaco, Total and Royal Dutch.
Bank Degroof rated the share a 'market outperformer' at 13,950 francs. It had short-term scope "because substantial upward earnings revisions give attractive P/E and P/CF ratios."

Earnings per share were up 65 percent in the first half of 1997 compared with the first half of 1996 as high volumes offset some margin and price declines. A 13 percent rise in the dollar and refining's recovery in Europe also helped earnings.
At broker Vermeulen Raemdonck analyst Francois Poullet expected PetroFina to post a 23 percent rise in 1997 EPS and four percent in 1998. He maintained his 'buy' rating.
He said the results of the refining-marketing-transport division would play a crucial role in PetroFina's performance.
Investments in the distribution network of PetroFina's Fina in the United States had contributed to the first half and the prospects remained good, he said.

Poullet expected PetroFina to benefit from a reducing tax burden in coming years as highly-taxed Norwegian production was replaced by output from lower-taxed centres such as the United States, Vietnam, Italy and the United Kingdom.
He remained cautious on chemicals, but said the focus on monomer production would help offset pressure on polymer prices.
Filip Platteeuw at KB Securities upgraded his EPS forecast to 965 francs. At a price of 14,000 francs this led to a 1997 P/E of 14.5. He rated the share an 'accumulate'.
"PetroFina has consistently outperformed the Bel-20 over the last year and we believe this to remain the case over the coming year," he said.
The outlook for plastics was favourable, he said, with high-density polyethylene prices and margins increasing and margins in polypropylene expected to improve.
Price increases were somewhat further away for polystyrene, Platteeuw said. In refining margins would ease back from the levels seen in the first half, but remain comparatively high.
